museum: Raclin Murphy Museum of Art, University of Notre Dame
address: St. Andre Way (corner of Eddy Street and Angela Blvd), Notre Dame, IN 46556

levels.summary: Entrance level: Grand Atrium, Welcome Desk, Ivan's Cafe, Book Shop, Learning Commons, Teaching Gallery, African Art, and European & American Art 1700-1900.

levels.hub: balcony that overlooks the Grand Atrium
levels.summary: Balcony level: European Art Through 1700, the Mary Queen of Families Chapel, Indigenous Art of the Americas (North American, Mesoamerican, Central & South American), Art of the Spanish Americas, Temporary Exhibitions, and the Founders Room.
Education level: Art Studio A and B and a flexible north space. No permanent collection galleries.
Lower Level: International Modern and Contemporary Art, the Sculpture Court, and the Object Study Room.

vertical_circulation.name: Vertical circulation
vertical_circulation.note: The elevator and the North and South stairs connect all four levels (Lower Level, Level 1, Level 2, Level 3). On Level 1 they open onto the Grand Atrium; on Level 2 onto the balcony.

spaces.name: Main Entrance
spaces.notes: The visitor entrance is at the south-center of Level 1 and leads directly into the Grand Atrium and Welcome Desk.

spaces.name: Grand Atrium
spaces.notes: The Grand Atrium is the central hall of Level 1; the North and South stairs and the elevator open onto it. It is open above to the Level 2 balcony.

spaces.name: Welcome Desk
spaces.notes: The Welcome Desk sits in the Grand Atrium just inside the entrance.

spaces.name: Coat Room
spaces.notes: The Coat Room is just east of the Welcome Desk.

spaces.name: Ivan's Cafe
spaces.notes: Ivan's Cafe is in the northwest of Level 1, off the Cafe Lobby, next to the Book Shop.

spaces.name: Book Shop
spaces.notes: The Book Shop is in the northwest of Level 1, beside Ivan's Cafe.

spaces.name: Cafe Lobby
spaces.notes: The Cafe Lobby is at the north-center of Level 1, linking the cafe/book shop to the atrium.

spaces.name: European and American Art 1700-1900
spaces.notes: This gallery occupies the entire east side of Level 1, wrapping around the atrium from the northeast to the southeast.

spaces.name: Restrooms (Level 1)
spaces.notes: Level 1 restrooms, including a Family Restroom, are on the east side off the Grand Atrium.

spaces.name: Learning Commons
spaces.notes: The Learning Commons is on the west side of Level 1.

spaces.name: Teaching Gallery
spaces.notes: The Teaching Gallery is in the southwest corner of Level 1, next to African Art.

spaces.name: African Art
spaces.pos: south (center-west, between the Teaching Gallery and the atrium)
spaces.notes: African Art is on the south side of Level 1, between the Teaching Gallery (west) and the Grand Atrium.

spaces.name: Balcony
spaces.notes: The Level 2 Balcony rings the open Grand Atrium; all Level 2 spaces open off it.

spaces.name: Temporary Exhibitions
spaces.notes: The Temporary Exhibitions galleries occupy the west and northwest of Level 2. Rotating/current exhibitions are shown here.

spaces.name: Founders Room
spaces.notes: The Founders Room (used for meetings) is at the north-center of Level 2, between Temporary Exhibitions and Indigenous Art.

spaces.name: Indigenous Art of the Americas
spaces.notes: Indigenous Art of the Americas is in the northeast of Level 2. Its North American sub-gallery is on the north side and its Mesoamerican sub-gallery toward the east; the Central and South American sub-gallery continues down the east side.

spaces.name: Central and South American (Indigenous Art)
spaces.notes: The Central and South American sub-gallery of Indigenous Art runs down the east side of Level 2, between the Mesoamerican gallery and Art of the Spanish Americas.

spaces.name: Art of the Spanish Americas
spaces.notes: Art of the Spanish Americas is in the southeast corner of Level 2, below the Central and South American gallery and next to the east wing of European Art Through 1700.

spaces.name: European Art Through 1700
spaces.pos: south (in two wings flanking the Chapel)
spaces.notes: European Art Through 1700 occupies the south side of Level 2 in two wings, a southwest wing and a southeast wing, that flank the Mary, Queen of Families Chapel.

spaces.name: Mary, Queen of Families Chapel
spaces.pos: south (center, between the two European Art Through 1700 wings)
spaces.notes: The Mary, Queen of Families Chapel is at the south-center of Level 2, centered between the two wings of European Art Through 1700, directly across the balcony from the Founders Room.

spaces.name: Restrooms (Level 2)
spaces.notes: Level 2 restrooms are on the east side off the balcony.

spaces.name: Art Studio A
spaces.notes: Art Studio A is on the south side of Level 3.

spaces.name: Art Studio B
spaces.notes: Art Studio B is on the south side of Level 3, east of Art Studio A.

spaces.name: Restrooms (Level 3)
spaces.notes: Level 3 restrooms are on the east side.

spaces.name: Level 3 Landing
spaces.notes: Level 3 is the education floor (art studios and a flexible north space); it has no permanent collection galleries.

spaces.name: Sculpture Court
spaces.notes: The Sculpture Court is at the north end of the Lower Level, adjoining the International Modern and Contemporary Art gallery.

spaces.name: International Modern and Contemporary Art
spaces.notes: The International Modern and Contemporary Art gallery is the central gallery of the Lower Level, with the Sculpture Court to its north and the Object Study Room to its south.

spaces.name: Object Study Room
spaces.notes: The Object Study Room is at the south end of the Lower Level.

spaces.name: Restrooms (Lower Level)
spaces.notes: Lower Level restrooms are in the center, off the International Modern and Contemporary Art gallery.
